A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SRS/SRSNet research. Their main text, equations, Tables 1–12, Figures 1–7, and Appendices A–B are readable and support a complete comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original SRSNet forecasting experiments, component ablations, plug-in evaluations, efficiency measurements, and sensitivity analyses in Section 5 and Appendix A.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results, including the detailed forecasting and ablation tables and case studies in Appendix A.

M1.justification: Sections 3–4 retain the same selective patching, dynamic reassembly, gradient handling, adaptive embedding fusion, SRSNet prediction head, and MSE training objective. The additional citations in Section 3 do not change the method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the four ETT subsets, Weather, Electricity, Solar, and Traffic, with identical coverage in the supplementary studies. Appendix B's new domain and task categories describe literature, without adding evaluations.

E2.justification: Tables 2 and 8 retain the same ten forecasting baselines. The plug-in comparisons retain MLP, PatchTST, Crossformer, PatchMLP, and xPatch; efficiency comparator membership also remains unchanged. Citation changes do not introduce evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The dataset splits, MSE/MAE metrics, forecasting horizons {96, 192, 336, 720}, best-result selection over look-back windows {96, 336, 512}, and TFB evaluation procedure are identical. The efficiency and sensitivity experiment settings are also unchanged.

E4.justification: The component ablations and plug-in studies, efficiency analyses, four hyperparameter sweeps in Figure 4, and selected-patch forecasting case studies in Figures 5–7 are retained without changes.

E5.justification: Both versions explicitly report SRSNet standard deviations calculated using five random seeds in Table 8. The run-count disclosure and uncertainty-reporting practice are unchanged, with no added statistical tests.

E6.justification: The numerical results, rankings, sensitivity curves, and appendix prediction plots are identical. For example, Table 2 retains SRSNet's ETTh1 average MSE/MAE of 0.404/0.424, and Table 8 retains its horizon-96 ETTh1 MSE of 0.366 ± 0.001.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, search-space counting argument, equations (1)–(16), and universal-approximation rationale are unchanged. No proofs or formal assumptions are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: adaptive selective representation spaces, the SRSNet construction and forecasting-performance claim, and SRS's ability to improve existing patch-based models.

C2.justification: The explanations of component effectiveness and efficiency remain identical. Section 6 retains the same limitations concerning non-patch models, foundation-model scaling, interpretability, and fusion-weight initialization, together with the same future directions.

D1.justification: Appendix A retains the same TFB evaluation information, PyTorch/Python 3.8 environment, NVIDIA Tesla-A800 hardware, Adam optimizer, and batch-size adjustment from 64 down to 8. Hyperparameter guidance and the resource link under the abstract are unchanged.

R1.justification: Appendix B introduces domain/task groupings and redistributes existing citations. Section 3 newly cites the hierarchical-classification forecasting paper and LangTime, both already cited in v1. Five distinct works, including TimeCMA and Time-o1, are removed; AutoCTS++ remains through its other entry. The central novelty positioning is retained.

P1.justification: The abstract and contributions correct 'plugin-and-play' to 'plug-and-play.' Appendix B gains an introductory domain/task paragraph and revises its citation-heavy opening. These are localized edits; the main narrative and section order remain intact.

P2.justification: Figures 1–7 and Tables 1–12 retain their designs, captions, and placement. Bibliography entries reflow across pages 12–16, and Appendix B's additional paragraph changes local text layout. There is no substantial visual redesign.

improvement.justification: Appendix B organizes v1's broad citation list more explicitly, but introduces misleading assignments: v4 cites Camel's compression paper for imputation and soccer-commentary and text-motion generation papers for energy. These mismatches are evident from the PDFs' own bibliography. They outweigh the small wording and organizational improvements, modestly weakening related-work accuracy while leaving the method and experimental evidence unchanged.
